[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] DartPoints own site describes a strategy of delivering enterprise grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure services to communities outside the largest United States metros, operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets. The company began operations in the early 2000s. DartPoints is headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas. This session refreshed and sharpened a prior research passes brief note that the company received a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025: per both DartPoints own press release and independent trade press corroboration from Data Center Dynamics, both fetched fresh this session, NOVA Infrastructure actually acquired majority control of DartPoints, announced April 30, 2025, with lending partner Orion Infrastructure Capital, committing more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital, while the prior owner, Astra Capital Management, retained a meaningful minority stake. As part of that same transaction, DartPoints acquired the underlying real estate for three of its data centers, in Greenville, South Carolina, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Asheville, North Carolina, per both sources. DartPoints own site lists 11 facilities across 10 markets, including Baton Rouge, Louisiana (2 facilities) and Shreveport, Louisiana, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, Columbus, Indiana, Asheville, North Carolina, and Columbia, Greenville, Charleston, and Spartanburg, South Carolina, matching every state where this registry lists a DartPoints facility, and DCD independently corroborates the same 11 facility, 10 market count and adds that the company serves more than 900 enterprise customers including Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems. The company emphasizes AI ready, high density infrastructure, 99.999 percent uptime, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. This specific row, the Greenville, South Carolina facility (internal code GSP01), per the operators own dedicated location page for this facility, fetched fresh this session, sits at 78 Global Dr # 100, Greenville, SC 29607. This is one of the three facilities, per the NOVA Infrastructure transaction sourcing above, whose underlying real estate DartPoints itself now owns following the April 2025 transaction, and is specifically named in that transactions own coverage.

reading.body:
DartPoints Greenville has a published IT load of 2.5 MW, equivalent to roughly 250 GPUs or TPUs at typical AI training density, making it the largest disclosed data center in South Carolina and 38 percent of the state's total published capacity.

The facility sits in a regional market outside the largest US metros, where DartPoints operates 11 locations across 10 markets. DartPoints acquired the underlying real estate for this property in April 2025 as part of a majority control acquisition by NOVA Infrastructure, a signal of capital commitment to regional infrastructure outside Tier 1 metros. The facility emphasizes AI-ready high-density infrastructure and SOC 2 Type II compliance, qualifying it for enterprise and institutional workloads requiring security attestation.

South Carolina has 14 mapped data center facilities but sparse published capacity across the state. Most facilities disclose no power specifications, making this facility's transparent 2.5 MW unusual for the region. Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on DartPoints' ability to expand beyond current capacity, which is not published. The data does not show whether Greenville's regional grid has room for substantial growth, or how much of DartPoints' 11-facility footprint across the Southeast has similar expansion potential.
